notes.text:
All Israel — Namely, their representatives. Shechem - To the city of Shechem, a place convenient for the purpose, not only because it was a Levitical city, and a city of refuge, and a place near Joshua's city, but especially for the two main ends for which he summoned them thither.

1. For the solemn burial of the bones of Joseph, and the rest of the patriarchs, for which this place was designed.

2. For the solemn renewing of their covenant with God; which in this place was first made between God and Abraham, Gen. xii, 6, 7, and afterwards renewed by the Israelites at their first entrance into the land of Canaan, between the two mountains of Ebal and Gerizzim, chap. viii, 30, &c. which were very near Shechem: and therefore this place was most proper, both to remind them of their former obligations to God, and to engage them to a farther ratification of them. Before God - As in God's presence, to hear what Joshua was to speak to them in God's name, and to receive God's commands from his mouth. He had taken a solemn farewell before: but as God renewed his strength, he desired to improve it for their good. We must never think our work for God done, 'till our life is done.

The people — To the elders, by whom it was to be imparted to all the rest, and to as many of the people as came thither. He spake to them in God's name, and as from him, in the language of a prophet, Thus saith the Lord. Jehovah, the great God, and the God of Israel, whom you are peculiarly engaged to hear. The flood - Or, the river, namely, Euphrates, so called by way of eminency. They served - That is, Both Abraham and Nahor were no less idolaters than the rest of mankind. This is said to prevent their vain boasting in their worthy ancestors, and to assure them that whatsoever good was in, or had been done by their progenitors, was wholly from God's free grace, and not for their own merit or righteousness.

I took — I snatched him out of that idolatrous place, and took him into acquaintance and covenant with myself, which was the highest honour and happiness he was capable of. And led - That is I brought him after his father's death into Canaan, Gen. xii, 1, and I conducted and preserved him in all his travels through the several parts of Canaan. And multiplied - That is, gave him a numerous posterity, not only by Hagar and Keturah, but even by Sarah and by Isaac. Gave Isaac - By my special power and grace to be heir of my covenant, and all my promises, and the seed in or by which all the nations were to be blessed.

glossa.text: *I took therefore your father.* ((AUG.)) In that the LXX have, etc., *as far as* which is the true seed of Abraham.

notes.text: My law — The doctrine which I am about to deliver. 2. Parable - Weighty sentences. Dark sayings - Not that the words are hard to be understood, but the things, God's transcendent goodness, their unparallel'd ingratitude; and their stupid ignorance and insensibleness, under such excellent teachings of God's word and works, are prodigious and hard to be believed. Of old - Of things done in ancient times.

Established — This is justly put in first place, as the chief of all his mercies. A testimony - His law, called a testimony, because it is a witness between God and men, declaring the duties which God expects from man, and the blessings which man may expect from God.

glossa.text: *Understanding.* ((AUG.)) Because these things narrated, etc., *as far as* the things that seem open are parables and riddles. *Attend.* ((CAS.)) First the Lord himself speaks, that reverence may grow. *My people,* who obey me. The mouth of God is Asaph, who spoke these things below: *How great things we have heard from the beginning.* Of the Old Testament: or, the faithful Synagogue reproaches the wicked.
*In parables.* ((AUG.)) Parables are likenesses of things. *Propositions.* Which in Greek are *problemata,* questions having something to be resolved.

*How great things.* ((CAS.)) He tells summarily what God did for the Jews: yet for men ungrateful to him, and thus, if not to them, it profits the sons nevertheless, lest they become as their fathers. ((AUG.)) First God spoke in a man, now the man himself: *How great things we have heard.* That foretold word God spoke from himself, lest his speech be despised.

*And he raised up,* etc. ((AUG.)) This testimony. *The beginning,* whence above: *I will utter propositions from the beginning.* The beginning is the Old Testament, the end the New. There is fear, which is the beginning: but here is Christ, *the end of the law unto righteousness to every one that believeth ((Rom. X))*, who gives the Spirit, whence: *Charity, which drives out fear ((I Joan. IV))* . The old law is called the testimony of this New Testament, because it has testimony from the law and the Prophets: whence that was called the tabernacle of testimony which prefigured so many mystical things: *Testimony* therefore the Old Testament is called in so far as it proves and testifies, law in so far as it commands. ((CASS., REM.)) *He raised up* the testimony as though dead in Adam, that is, the law; or, while it is written down it is raised up, having been lulled asleep before by ignorance. *A testimony in Jacob,* this perhaps is that Jacob, having wrestled with the angel, went halt when his thigh was touched: which signifies that the Jews partly stand fast in faith, partly depart from salvation: and so what befell Jacob was a testimony of this thing. Behold a parable. *To their sons.* And these same sons are another generation, namely the people of grace.
*Another generation.* Through the generations the commandments of God were handed on, lest any think them given to one only.

*That they may set.* This is the profit of the fathers' preaching. *Let them seek out.* ((AUG.)) Those who were said above to have known, now *let them seek out,* that hoping in God they may be helped by him to fulfil it.

notes.text: Now — Herein the efficacy of Christianity greatly appears, - that it neither takes away nor embitters, but sweetly tempers, that most refined of all affections, our desire of or love to the dead.
So — As God raised him. With him - With their living head.

By the word of the Lord — By a particular Revelation. We who are left - This intimates the fewness of those who will be then alive, compared to the multitude of the dead. Believers of all ages and nations make up, as it were, one body; in consideration of which, the believers of that age might put themselves in the place, and speak in the person, of them who were to live till the coming of the Lord. Not that St. Paul hereby asserted (though some seem to have imagined so) that the day of the Lord was at hand.

With a shout — Properly, a proclamation made to a great multitude. Above this is, the voice of the archangel; above both, the trumpet of God; the voice of God, somewhat analogous to the sound of a trumpet.
Together — In the same moment. In the air - The wicked will remain beneath, while the righteous, being absolved, shall be assessors with their Lord in the judgment. With the Lord - In heaven.

glossa.text: *Through Jesus will he bring with him.* Ever going on, by following him they came to the sleep of death, whence also it is written in another Epistle: *We who live.*

*Them.* Not only those who shall be found alive, but also the dead, concerning whom you doubt. *Who have slept.* He calls Christ dead, the faithful sleeping, that they may the more believe the resurrection: he calls Christ dead, that when we have heard that he died and rose again, we also may hope that we shall rise again through the power of his divinity.

*For the Lord himself.* In his own person.

*With the trumpet of God. ((ANSELM.))* This trumpet will rouse all and will terrify the enemies, will summon his own to battle, that they may vanquish the adversaries, and that [the adversaries] may flee from the face of the Lord and be sent into hell. And again, as the trumpet once called together the people of the Hebrews on the feasts: so this trumpet will call together the people of the saints to the solemnity of eternal gladness, God, he says, commanding, and with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God sounding. *He shall descend.* Not lowly as before, but commanding with a voice, either his own or the archangel's, or the angels', by which he will make the dead rise again, which is called a trumpet, because it is manifest, or as though for battle, which shall be God's and Christ's, to which God will give efficacy.
*In the clouds.* Because a cloud will take them up, as it took up Christ at the ascension, whence another interpreter says: *With bearing clouds.*

notes.text: Then shall the kingdom of heaven — That is, the candidates for it, be like ten virgins - The bridemaids on the wedding night were wont to go to the house where the bride was, with burning lamps or torches in their hands, to wait for the bride groom's coming. When he drew near, they went to meet him with their lamps, and to conduct him to the bride.

The foolish took no oil with them — No more than kept them burning just for the present. None to supply their future want, to recruit their lamp's decay. The lamp is faith. A lamp and oil with it, is faith working by love.
The wise took oil in their vessels — Love in their hearts. And they daily sought a fresh supply of spiritual strength, till their faith was made perfect.
While the bridegroom delayed — That is, before they were called to attend him, they all slumbered and slept - Were easy and quiet, the wise enjoying a true, the foolish a false peace.
At midnight — In an hour quite unthought of.
They trimmed their lamps — They examined themselves and prepared to meet their God.

Give us of your oil, for our lamps are gone out — Our faith is dead. What a time to discover this! Whether it mean the time of death, or of judgment. Unto which of the saints wilt thou then turn? Who can help thee at such a season?

But the wise answered, Lest there be not enough for us and you! — Beginning the sentence with a beautiful abruptness; such as showed their surprise at the state of those poor wretches, who had so long received them, as well as their own souls. Lest there be not enough - It is sure there is not; for no man has more than holiness enough for himself. Go ye rather to them that sell - Without money and without price: that is, to God, to Christ. And buy - If ye can. O no! The time is past and returns no more!
Watch therefore — He that watches has not only a burning lamp, but likewise oil in his vessel. And even when he sleepeth, his heart waketh. He is quiet; but not secure.

glossa.text: *Ten virgins.* The virgins are all who refrain themselves from the luxury of the world. *And the bride.* All together are the bride, who has now been espoused a virgin away from the corruption of the world. She shall be wedded, when the mortal shall be joined to the immortal.
*Five.* Because continence in carnal enticements is fivefold, namely that in the five senses they should refrain themselves from pleasures.
*And the bridegroom tarrying.* Because there is no little time between the first and the second coming of Christ. *They all slumbered and slept.* Because they are afterwards to be raised up.
*And at midnight there was a cry made.* That is, with no one knowing or hoping for it. Whence *The day of the Lord shall come as a thief in the night ((I Thess. III))*.

*Give us of your oil,* etc. Those whose deeds are propped up by what is another's fail when that same praise is withdrawn, and out of habit they always seek that whence the mind is wont to rejoice. And so they wish to have before God, who is the searcher of the heart, the testimony of men, who do not see hearts.

*They are going out.* That is, at the coming of the judge they are darkened within, and they have no reward from God, because they have received their praise.

*Lest perhaps.* Because each shall render an account for himself, nor is anyone helped before God by another's testimony, since to him secret things lie open, and each scarcely suffices for himself, that his own conscience may bear him witness. *Lest perhaps* each one shall receive a reward for his own works, nor in the day of judgment can the virtues of some relieve the vices of others. *To them that sell.* They that sell are flatterers, because they give praise and receive some reward.

*But whilst.* While they bend themselves toward the things that are without, and seek their accustomed joys, since they have not known the things within, he comes who judges. *It was shut.* After the judgment great is the severity of him whose mercy before it is unspeakable.

*But last of all.* By true penance, by fruitless tears, those left outside knock. It is not said that they bought oil: because, no joy from the praises of others now remaining, in their straits they return to the imploring of God.

*Watch ye.* Namely, that we may prepare for ourselves the testimony of a good conscience, lest with the foolish virgins we remain outside. *You know not the day nor the hour.* Not only the day of judgment, but the day of each man's death, or the hour in which he who is found ready shall then also be found ready. And because he desires to find us ready, he adds another parable on the same matter.

glossa.text: *Love them,* etc., *and you shall have discipline.* He that loves wisdom keeps discipline in his manners. For he does not love wisdom who does not keep discipline. Whence: *If you love me, keep my commandments ((Joan. XIV))*.
*She preventeth them that covet her.* Offering herself freely. For he himself is *the way, the truth, and the life ((Joan. XIV))*: through him one goes, unto him one strives, to him one attains.

*Her sitting by,* etc. Ever ready, that is, to help, whence: *Behold, I stand at the door and knock, if any man shall open to me, I will go in to him and will sup with him, and he with me ((Apoc. III))* . In the present life wisdom must be studied, and life led according to the rule of her discipline.

registers.label: Spare
lines: At midnight the cry went up: the bridegroom is coming!
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
Wisdom is radiant and is found by those who seek her.
We watch for the Lord with longing hearts.
We do not know the day or the hour.
So we keep awake, and keep the oil ready.
Come, let us worship while the lamps still burn.
We come, watching for the Bridegroom. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: It is the middle of the night, the oil running low, the wedding torches guttering — and then a shout splits the dark: the bridegroom is coming, go out to meet him.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
Wisdom is bright and never fades; she is found sitting at the gate by all who rise early to seek her.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
So we watch through the long night, longing, awake, our flasks of oil close at hand.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
We do not know the day or the hour, but we know the One we are waiting for.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning.
So come, wise and watchful, into the light, and worship.
Keep your lamps trimmed and burning. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: At midnight the cry: the bridegroom is here!
Keep your lamps burning.
Wisdom is found by all who seek her early.
Keep your lamps burning.
We do not know the day or the hour.
Keep your lamps burning.
Come, let us worship while the oil still lasts.
We come, watching for the Bridegroom. Amen.
